chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Secretive charity extinguishes the wrath of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted.'

key_terms.تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى: Blessed and Exalted — honorific epithet for God, affirming His transcendence and sanctity
key_terms.تُطْفِئُ: Extinguishes — vivid metaphor of fire being put out, indicating the quenching of divine wrath
key_terms.صَدَقَةُ السِّرِّ: Secretive/private charity — almsgiving done quietly without public display, contrasted with public charity
key_terms.غَضَبَ الرَّبِّ: The wrath/anger of the Lord — divine displeasure, an attribute mentioned in the Quran and hadith

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet say about giving charity in secret in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) narrates this prophetic tradition in which the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) teaches that giving charity in secret has the remarkable spiritual effect of extinguishing divine anger. This hadith reflects the Shia tradition's emphasis on sincerity (ikhlas) in worship — that acts done privately, without seeking public acclaim, carry special weight before God. In the early Muslim community, this teaching encouraged believers to give charity with pure intention, knowing that even a small gift given secretly could ward off divine displeasure.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Al Waleed Al Wassafy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The secretive charity extinguishes the Anger of the Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, Blessed and High’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafiy who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said,
’Giving charity out of public sight extinguishes the anger of the Lord, Allah, the most Blessed, the most High.’”
